title: Strategic Sync Protocol — OKR Release-Banding & Initiative Interlock Canvas
creator: Nora Patel
description: Problem: cross-functional initiatives drift from company-level outcomes because teams use different cadence terms, have mismatched acceptance gates, and lack an explicit escalation path. Goal: introduce a lightweight operational protocol (Strategic Sync Protocol) that 1) groups initiatives into release-bands by risk and customer impact, 2) uses a single Initiative Interlock Canvas to capture dependencies and owners, and 3) defines an escalation ladder and timeboxed remediation flow for misaligned commitments. This ticket scopes the PM playbook, templates, and a pilot across Platform, Console, and Dedicated teams.
acceptance_criteria: Interlock Canvas template stored in Confluence and referenced from all company-level initiative pages
All company-targeted initiatives for Q1 are assigned a release-band (Tier A / Tier B / Tier C) with justification
Cross-functional alignment session run for each release-band with documented decisions and follow-ups
Escalation ladder documented with 3 tiers: Team, Program, Executive and a 7-day remediation SLA for Tier A blockers
Rollout pilot completed with at least 4 initiatives and feedback incorporated into final playbook
success_metrics: % initiatives with Interlock Canvas completed >= 95% by pilot end
Median time to resolve cross-team blockers reduced from 14 days to <= 5 days for Tier A
Stakeholder alignment score (post-session survey) >= 4.0 / 5 across pilot participants
Number of unreconciled OKR vs initiative mappings at quarter boundary <= 2
stakeholders: Maya Thompson - Head of Product Strategy
milestones: 2026-02-17: Draft Interlock Canvas and release-banding rubric
2026-02-24: Cross-functional pilot kickoff and alignment workshops

2026-03-31: Company-wide announcement and onboarding materials published
decisions: Use three release-bands (Tier A - mission critical, Tier B - strategic, Tier C - exploratory) instead of percent-based gating to keep language explanatory for execs and teams
Anchor acceptance gates to lead indicators (e.g., infra readiness, model validation milestones) rather than only milestone dates
Require a named escalation contact for every initiative and an explicit remediation owner for each blocker
risks: Teams perceive release-banding as additional bureaucracy; mitigation: keep Canvas <1 page and make templates copy/paste friendly
Insufficient executive bandwidth to enforce remediation SLA on Tier A; mitigation: limit Tier A to <10 initiatives and escalate proactively
Overlap with existing cadence artifacts (planning boards, release trains); mitigation: map Canvas fields to existing templates and auto-link
